invariants.rationale: Builder evidence describes a compatible profile, but only host preflight can identify the concrete executable variants, helpers, kernel support, and process confinement selected for this launch.

diagnostic.remediation: Select a host and registered implementation bundle matching every pinned component, feature, helper, confinement, kernel, and conformance requirement; do not fall back.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from non-setuid Bubblewrap, Firecracker jailer, and Cloud Hypervisor outer-confinement requirements.

invariants.title: Dynamic filesystem source changes after preflight
invariants.statement: Every dynamic filesystem source is safely resolved to an object identity retained through target attachment; validation by pathname followed by a later pathname reopen is forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The concrete source exists only on the selected host. Retaining its verified object identity across the preflight-to-driver handoff is required to prevent path replacement and symlink traversal races.

diagnostic.remediation: Resolve the source safely, retain a descriptor or equivalent stable object handle through attachment, and reject any identity change.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Bubblewrap FD-bind support and Cloud Hypervisor trusted-caller path-resolution requirements.

invariants.title: Snapshot or restore violates its proven compatibility envelope
invariants.statement: Every snapshot or restore operation revalidates the exact captured component set, external-storage state, device state, secret treatment, quiescing state, VMM/driver/guest/kernel/CPU compatibility, and clone identity refresh required by the advertised snapshot class.
invariants.rationale: The Artifact and member can define and advertise a snapshot class, but only the live-operation boundary knows resident secrets, current devices/storage, quiescing, restore host, and clone count.

diagnostic.remediation: Quiesce and scrub as required, use a compatible restore envelope, rebind runtime identities, and refresh clone identity state before capture or resume.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor component, compatibility, secret, and clone-safety limitations.

invariants.title: Provider transfer substitutes an unverifiable object
invariants.statement: Provider transport preserves portable semantic identity and verifies selected member bytes or the OCI descriptor graph by digest after upload, download, and every cache hit; provider object IDs, aliases, tags, paths, and cache keys remain non-semantic metadata.
invariants.rationale: The selected member identity is known earlier, but only provider preflight can observe the transferred or cached object returned for this request and verify its content graph.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the provider object and transfer or fetch the exact member or OCI descriptor graph by verified content identity.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C provider research; transport is explicitly not a target profile.

invariants.title: Provider-side construction lacks equivalence evidence
invariants.statement: Provider-side construction may claim portable conformance only through a versioned product construction protocol with complete pinned inputs, suppressed provider defaults, a returned output identity, provenance, and member-bound semantic and runtime conformance evidence.
invariants.rationale: The versioned construction protocol and pinned input set are known when remote target-member construction begins. The provider output identity and evidence exist at N1 and must be verified before a member is published or can reach manifest verification at C0.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the versioned product construction protocol and require pinned inputs, explicit default suppression, output identity, provenance, and conformance evidence; otherwise expose the provider path as explicitly non-conforming.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet C from Modal/E2B-style provider construction boundaries.

invariants.title: Frontend dependency closure is mutable or incomplete
invariants.statement: Every semantic import, module, resource, external reader, fallback, and native source input belongs to one transitively immutable, content-pinned, provenance-recorded dependency closure that evaluates offline deterministically.
invariants.rationale: A frontend can identify its complete semantic dependency closure at P1; canonical publication at W0 is the latest safe boundary for independently verifying that closure and its identity.

diagnostic.remediation: Pin and record the complete transitive dependency closure, remove ambient readers and fallback imports, and evaluate offline.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D frontend and Nix composition research.

invariants.title: Composition provenance is incomplete
invariants.statement: Normalized composition provenance records every winning, losing, default, profile, import, override, native, and migration contributor with immutable identity and semantic role while excluding display-only source spans and order from the semantic digest.
invariants.rationale: All contributors and their roles are known after final Artifact composition at A1 and must be complete before canonical publication at W0.

diagnostic.remediation: Regenerate provenance from the complete contribution ledger and keep display-only locations outside the semantic digest.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D strongest-bypass analysis.

invariants.title: Extension effect projection is incomplete
invariants.statement: Every extension used by a conforming Artifact has a registered versioned closed contract and a total product-derived effect projection into the common field/profile and identity models; opaque or unprojectable effects cannot produce conforming types or claims.
invariants.rationale: Extension scope and declared effects are known at A1; target construction at N0 is the last boundary with both the resolved native value and the complete Packet C realization model.

diagnostic.remediation: Use a registered extension with a complete product-derived effect projection or emit an explicitly non-conforming output type.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D native-surface analysis.

invariants.title: Frontend translation is lossy or permissive
invariants.statement: Every renderer-to-wire adaptation is versioned and total over the semantic schema and fails closed on unknown, omitted, unserializable, rounded, duplicated, or reinterpreted values.
invariants.rationale: Only the W0 adapter boundary has both the rendered frontend value and the exact current wire schema, so it must prove a lossless total translation before canonicalization.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the version-matched total adapter and reject every value that cannot be represented exactly in the canonical schema.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D by tracing the comparison portable-value projection.

invariants.title: Canonical decoding is unbounded or accepts an invalid domain
invariants.statement: Canonical decoding rejects malformed syntax, trailing bytes, invalid UTF-8, unsupported numeric or Unicode representations, excessive nesting, and oversized input before semantic interpretation; WIRE-001 separately owns duplicate-object-key rejection.
invariants.rationale: Raw bytes and configured decoder bounds first meet at W0, and no partial or implementation-dependent interpretation may cross that boundary.

diagnostic.remediation: Encode one bounded canonical document in the supported byte, numeric, and Unicode domain.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D raw-wire boundary analysis.

invariants.title: Schema migration is ambiguous or non-idempotent
invariants.statement: Each supported old schema version has one versioned deterministic migration that validates old input first, preserves or explicitly rejects extension data, validates the current result, and is idempotent; downgrade, fallback chains, and frontend-owned migration are forbidden.
invariants.rationale: The original version and complete decoded old value first meet the product-owned migration registry at W0, where migration must finish before current canonical validation.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the single registered source-to-current migration and resolve every loss, ambiguity, or unsupported extension explicitly.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D migration-boundary analysis.

invariants.title: Native handle identity is incomplete
invariants.statement: A native handle identity binds the complete pinned transitive source graph, registry namespace and version, export attribute, native interface version, target system, affected member, and expected semantic effect; one registry-file digest or a current store path is insufficient.
invariants.rationale: The complete native registry, transitive Nix source closure, target system, export contract, and affected member first meet at N0 and must be bound before derivation construction.

diagnostic.remediation: Regenerate the typed handle identity over the complete transitive source and interface tuple for the exact target system and affected member.

invariants.notes: Discovered during Gate 2A Packet D by tracing the native-handle prototype identity domain.

invariants.title: Operator Configuration dependency closure is mutable or incomplete
invariants.statement: Operator Configuration dependency closure is mutable, incomplete, ambient, or not reproducible offline.
invariants.rationale: OC0 is the first boundary with the fully composed Operator Configuration and its dependency closure; it must reject non-reproducible or ambient composition before admission.

diagnostic.remediation: Pin every dependency, evaluate offline without ambient inputs, and submit the closed result to OC0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Operator Configuration precedence or provenance is ambiguous
invariants.statement: Operator composition precedence or contributor provenance is ambiguous, incomplete, or permits a force-class bypass.
invariants.rationale: OC0 is the first boundary with the complete Operator contributor ledger and precedence result; it must reject ambiguity and force-class bypasses there.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare every contributor and precedence decision, and reject undeclared force-class overrides at OC0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Operator Configuration escapes final validation
invariants.statement: A native/freeform source escape constructs validated Operator Configuration without the OC0 validator.
invariants.rationale: OC0 is the only boundary that can turn a fully composed Operator candidate into validated configuration; native/freeform input cannot bypass it.

diagnostic.remediation: Route native/freeform input through OC0; only the validator may construct validated Operator Configuration.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Managed-Service Definition dependency closure is mutable or incomplete
invariants.statement: Managed-Service Definition dependency closure is mutable, incomplete, ambient, or not reproducible offline.
invariants.rationale: MS0 is the first boundary with the fully composed Managed-Service Definition and its dependency closure; it must reject non-reproducible or ambient composition before translation.

diagnostic.remediation: Pin every dependency, evaluate offline without ambient inputs, and submit the closed result to MS0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Service precedence or provenance is ambiguous
invariants.statement: Service composition precedence or contributor provenance is ambiguous, incomplete, or permits a force-class bypass.
invariants.rationale: MS0 is the first boundary with the complete Service contributor ledger and precedence result; it must reject ambiguity and force-class bypasses there.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare every contributor and precedence decision, and reject undeclared force-class overrides at MS0.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Managed-Service Definition escapes final validation or the Core API
invariants.statement: A native/freeform source escape constructs a validated Managed-Service Definition or direct driver action without MS0 and the typed Core API.
invariants.rationale: MS0 is the only boundary that can turn a fully composed Service candidate into a validated definition; native/freeform input cannot bypass it or invoke a driver directly.

diagnostic.remediation: Route native/freeform input through MS0 and the typed Core API; direct driver action is unsupported.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Serialized resolved-stage envelope is open or ambiguously decoded
invariants.statement: A serialized resolved-stage envelope is open, unbounded, ambiguously decoded, unsupported, or accepted without strict versioned decoding.
invariants.rationale: RW0 is the first boundary with the serialized reentry envelope; strict bounded versioned decoding must reject it before replay.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the closed, bounded, versioned reentry envelope and strictly decode it at RW0 before full replay.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Reentry mints a private validated runtime stage
invariants.statement: Deserialization, copying, a cache hit, or a foreign object mints a private validated runtime stage.
invariants.rationale: RW0 bytes can produce only an untrusted candidate; C0 is the first product constructor permitted to mint a fresh private stage after complete replay.

diagnostic.remediation: Strictly decode and fully replay the reentry candidate; mint a private stage only through the C0 product constructor.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: PreparedLaunch identity fails to rederive upstream bindings
invariants.statement: PreparedLaunch identity omits or fails to rederive an earlier product identity, registration, admission, or retained-object binding.
invariants.rationale: D0 is the final preparation boundary with the current retained-object bindings and the complete PreparedLaunch identity; it must rederive them before driver use.

diagnostic.remediation: Rederive PreparedLaunch identity from every upstream product identity, registration, admission, and retained-object binding.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Driver accepts non-private or raw configuration input
invariants.statement: A driver accepts anything other than the product-owned private PreparedLaunch stage or accepts raw/backend-default configuration as input.
invariants.rationale: D0 is the driver-entry boundary; only the product-owned private PreparedLaunch type is admissible and raw/backend-default input has no supported construction path.

diagnostic.remediation: Invoke drivers only with the product-owned private PreparedLaunch and reject direct, raw, copied, deserialized, or backend-default input before mutation.

invariants.notes: Registered for Packet D resource-composition and driver-boundary correction; hook and test locations remain planned until prototype tracing.

invariants.title: Authoritative Core commit by a stale authority epoch
invariants.statement: Every authoritative Core-state commit validates the complete capability of Sandbox ID, runtime epoch, and authority epoch against the durable authority high-water mark and commits only under the current authority epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the presented capability triple and the durable authority high-water mark, both Core records requiring no external probe. Q2: authority fencing is Core. Q3: D0 is the effect-commit boundary and the last station where refusing still prevents an obsolete actor's write from becoming authoritative. Q4: the commit belongs to whichever actor presents the capability, so this entry is authoritative at D0 with defensive revalidation hooks at R0, R1, L1, E1, and T0.

diagnostic.remediation: Validate the full capability against the current authority epoch before every authoritative commit and reject stale holders.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges IDENTITY-04, IDENTITY-03. Traversal: driver effect-commit traversal, defensively revalidated at every later commit station.

invariants.title: Successor effect authority granted without fencing or drain proof
invariants.statement: The Core grants a successor actor effect authority only after the target is proven, for this exact handoff, to validate the fencing token atomically or to provide a product-verifiable predecessor drain or termination boundary.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the current external target's fencing and drain capability for this handoff plus the predecessor's outstanding authority; the target capability is external state the product does not own, which is what makes this a preflight rather than a boundary rejection. Q2: granting effect authority is Core. Q3: D0 is the last station before the successor could produce an effect. Q4: the grant is made on this traversal before the successor acts, so it is not deferred to the successor's own traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Prove atomic target fencing or a verifiable predecessor drain for the handoff, or quarantine and reconcile instead of granting authority.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges IDENTITY-21. Traversal: authority handoff preflight traversal preceding driver dispatch.

invariants.title: Driver claims exclusive effect authority without target fencing support
invariants.statement: A driver declares for each effect boundary it exposes whether the target validates its fencing token atomically or offers a verifiable drain boundary, and refuses to dispatch an exclusive effect when it can prove neither.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the target's current fencing behaviour and the driver's declared effect contract, checked immediately before dispatch; validity turns on current external state, so this is a preflight. Q2: the effect boundary and its fencing mechanics are the driver/provider boundary. Q3: D0, because after dispatch exclusivity can no longer be established. Q4: the driver commits the violation on its own dispatch traversal, distinct from the Core grant that precedes it.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare the fencing mechanism per effect boundary and refuse exclusive dispatch when neither atomic fencing nor a verifiable drain exists.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges IDENTITY-21, LIFECYCLE-42. Traversal: driver dispatch traversal.

invariants.title: Unfenced handoff reported as a definite outcome
invariants.statement: When a handoff cannot establish exclusive effect authority, the affected resources are quarantined or reconciled and the Operation retains its ambiguous terminal outcome rather than a definite success or failure.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the post-handoff evidence about whether the predecessor can still act, which exists only after the launch or handoff has run; the outcome is therefore provable only from observed conformance. Q2: terminal outcomes are Core. Q3: R1 is the terminalization station on this traversal and the last point at which a definite outcome can be withheld. Q4: reconciliation and adoption resolving the ambiguity are filed at exactly this phase, since origin is attribution rather than an information set.

diagnostic.remediation: Quarantine or reconcile the affected resources and publish the ambiguity variant naming the fencing proof Core lacks.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges IDENTITY-22, IDENTITY-09. Traversal: launch, handoff, and reconciliation terminalization traversal.

invariants.title: Driver retry or adoption without native idempotency or exact adoption proof
invariants.statement: A driver retries the same external effect only under the provider's own idempotency token for that effect and adopts an existing external execution only with exact proof of its external identity, target, runtime epoch, and fencing.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared effect class, the provider's currently available idempotency token, and the discoverable external identity; these depend on current external provider state, so the check is a preflight decided before mutation. Q2: native idempotency and adoption identity live at the driver/provider boundary. Q3: D0, because after dispatch a blind retry has already duplicated the effect. Q4: this is the driver half of a two-owner seam whose Core half records the recovery classification on its own traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Retry only with the provider's own idempotency token, adopt only under exact identity and fencing proof, and otherwise reconcile.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges RESULT-19, LIFECYCLE-43. Traversal: driver retry and adoption traversal.

invariants.title: Provider status alone justifies a Core outcome
invariants.statement: Every driver declares which native identities, state observations, fencing results, and supervision facts justify each Core outcome variant it may report, and reports no variant whose declared evidence it did not obtain.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the driver's declared evidence contract and the evidence actually held, both complete at the decoding boundary and independent of any later observation. Q2: the evidence contract belongs to the driver/provider boundary. Q3: D0 is where a variant is selected, so it is the last station at which an unjustified variant can be refused. Q4: the driver commits the violation; the separate rule that provider acknowledgement is not the Core postcondition is a different fact set on the launch traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare required evidence per outcome variant and map status-only responses to the ambiguity variant instead.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges RESULT-43, RESULT-50. Traversal: driver evidence-decoding and outcome-selection traversal.

invariants.title: Start authorizes a launch without fencing the prior runtime epoch
invariants.statement: A Start commits its launch authorization only after the Sandbox's prior runtime epoch is permanently fenced, so no predecessor authority can commit Core state or act against the new epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the prior runtime epoch's fencing record and the launch authorization about to be committed, both Core durable records at the acceptance commit. Q2: authority fencing and lane grants are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so the owner is `core` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the acceptance commit and the last station at which an unfenced authorization can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the Start's own acceptance commit. Filed under L0.D0.

diagnostic.remediation: Permanently fence the prior runtime epoch and its authority before committing the Start's launch authorization.

invariants.notes: Packet E FEN family; discharges LIFECYCLE-04, IDENTITY-03. Traversal: StartSandbox live-mutation traversal, at acceptance commit.

invariants.title: Sandbox identity reused across lifetimes
invariants.statement: Every Sandbox ID identifies exactly one Sandbox lifetime and is never allocated again, including by re-creation after Delete, restore-as-create, or Fork child allocation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: deciding reuse needs only the durable Sandbox-identity allocation record and the identity this acceptance proposes to commit; both are complete at the creation acceptance station and need no later input. Q2: durable identity records are Core. Q3: C0 is the last station on this traversal at which refusing still prevents a second lifetime binding to one ID, because every downstream station already treats the ID as committed. Q4: the offending act is the Create that allocates, so it stays on the create traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Allocate a fresh never-issued Sandbox ID for every new Sandbox lifetime and never rebind a retired one.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-01, TAXONOMY-38, LIFECYCLE-46. Traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal, including restore-as-create and Fork child allocation.

invariants.title: Create omits its initial runtime-epoch record
invariants.statement: Every accepted Create durably records either the runtime epoch allocated for a runtime-creating Create or an explicit absence of any runtime epoch for a Create that ends stopped.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested initial runtime disposition and the epoch allocation performed at acceptance; nothing observed after launch changes which of the two records is correct. Q2: epoch allocation and the durable Operation record are Core. Q3: C0 is the last station where the record can still be written as part of the acceptance commit; after C0 an absent epoch record is indistinguishable from a lost one. Q4: this is the Create's own traversal, not the launch it authorizes.

diagnostic.remediation: Record epoch one for a runtime-creating Create and an explicit no-runtime marker for a stopped Create.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-01, IDENTITY-23, LIFECYCLE-46. Traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Sandbox name reused before the former Sandbox is released
invariants.statement: A Create accepts a Sandbox name only when no undeleted Sandbox holds that name and the prior holder's reservation has been released by Delete.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested alias and the current name-reservation table, both complete at the create request surface. Q2: the name-reservation table and its release on Delete are the control plane's own durable records, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: C0, because after acceptance the alias is already bound and two lifetimes would share it. Q4: the retention ruling places an obligation whose subject is a later, different operation on that operation's own traversal, so a Create reusing an unreleased name is filed here rather than on the Delete that retains the reservation.

diagnostic.remediation: Choose a different alias, or delete the holding Sandbox and let its reservation release before reusing the name.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-01, LIFECYCLE-17. Traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Runtime epoch reused within a Sandbox
invariants.statement: Every runtime epoch is a positive, strictly increasing, never-reused integer within its Sandbox ID, durably committed before the launch it authorizes and consumed even when that launch fails or ends ambiguously.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Sandbox's durable epoch high-water mark and the epoch this acceptance proposes; the launch outcome is irrelevant because failed epochs are still consumed. Q2: epoch allocation is a Core durable record, not a request-surface fact, which is why the admission half of Start and Restore is filed separately under live. Q3: L1 is the commit that publishes the epoch; refusing later would mean a stale handle could not be distinguished from a later launch. Q4: the allocation is committed on the live request traversal, so it is not borrowed onto the launch traversal it authorizes.

diagnostic.remediation: Allocate the next unused epoch for the Sandbox and durably commit it before any effect that can create that runtime.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-01, IDENTITY-03, LIFECYCLE-46. Traversal: live Sandbox request traversal that allocates a runtime epoch (Start, same-Sandbox Restore, Fork); the Create-`running` epoch is covered by the C0 entry..

invariants.title: Exec request without a complete Sandbox runtime reference
invariants.statement: Every Exec request carries a complete Sandbox runtime reference naming the exact Sandbox ID and runtime epoch the execution is intended for.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Exec request's own coordinates, complete at the execution request surface. Q2: the Exec request surface owns request shape. Q3: E0, because the Process record commits the binding at the next station. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so this cannot be folded into the live-surface rule that names the same coordinate.

diagnostic.remediation: Populate both the Sandbox ID and runtime epoch on every Exec request from the observed handle.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-05, LIFECYCLE-24. Traversal: Exec request traversal.

invariants.title: Stale runtime reference silently retargeted
invariants.statement: A live request whose expected runtime epoch differs from the current epoch returns a typed stale-runtime result naming the requested Sandbox and expected epoch, and is never applied to the replacement runtime.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the request's expected epoch and the Sandbox's current durable epoch; both are Core records requiring no external probe, so this is not a dynamic preflight. Q2: the current-epoch record is a Core durable fact consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible live request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, the admission station, because acceptance is already the retargeting. Q4: the silent retarget would be committed by this same live request.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the typed stale-runtime result and require an explicit handle refresh instead of resolving to the current runtime.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-03, IDENTITY-06. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation request traversal.

invariants.title: Exec silently applied to a replacement runtime
invariants.statement: An Exec whose referenced runtime epoch is no longer current returns a typed stale-runtime result and is never admitted against the replacement runtime.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Exec's referenced epoch and the Sandbox's current durable epoch. Q2: the current-epoch record is a Core durable fact consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible Exec request at the exec request surface, so the owner is `exec`. Q3: E0, because the Process record is bound at the next station and a bound Process cannot be un-retargeted. Q4: the exec traversal never traverses L0, so filing the live-surface entry here would emit a false coverage claim; this is a separate entry on the exec traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the Exec with the typed stale-runtime result and require the caller to obtain a handle for the current runtime.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-03, IDENTITY-06. Traversal: Exec request traversal.

invariants.title: Coordinate substituted for another on the live request surface
invariants.statement: Each live request coordinate keeps its own declared domain: a name alias resolves once to an ID-pinned handle and never persists as identity; a representation etag guards only the representation revision and neither satisfies nor is satisfied by an expected-runtime-epoch precondition; an event or output cursor is an observation position only and is accepted in no identity, target, precondition, or authority position; an idempotency key is a recovery coordinate only; and a runtime epoch is expressible only as an expected-value precondition and never as an assignable field.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the fact is the declared type of each request coordinate at the boundary that decodes it, complete at the live request surface. Q2: owner was `core` in the drafts and moves to `live` under Criterion O, because the fact is the declared type of each request coordinate at its own caller station. Q3: L0 is the decoding station and the last point at which a wrong-domain coordinate can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's live request. Merged from indices 9, 10, and 11 (L2.D12 -- four entries, one owner, one station, two contradictory dispositions -- plus the L0.D2 output-cursor half). The 10-vs-11 reject/unrepresentable disagreement resolves to reject-at-boundary: raw wire frames, native extensions, and adapter ingress can still present a wrong-domain coordinate. Index 48 (OPA, canonical request identity includes transport or presentation fields) is not merged -- its fact set is the composition of the canonical digest backing the idempotency binding, a Core durable record rather than a coordinate domain, so it stays separate at `core`, L0->L0. The Process-ID / output-cursor half is not filed here, because output cursors live at `process.status.output.cursor` on the exec branch and L0 and E1 are mutually unreachable; it becomes A5.

diagnostic.remediation: Resolve the alias once and pin the returned Sandbox ID; evaluate etag and expected runtime epoch as independent preconditions; carry cursors only in observation requests.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-06, IDENTITY-07. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation and observation request traversal.

invariants.title: Snapshot manifest digest substituted for Snapshot identity
invariants.statement: Every Snapshot-targeted operation identifies its target by Snapshot ID, and the manifest digest remains an integrity coordinate that resolves no resource.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the declared Snapshot target variant, complete at the live request surface. Q2: the Snapshot target union is a Core control-plane fact, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible Snapshot-targeted request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, the station that decodes the sealed target. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because the Snapshot target admits only a Snapshot ID, and distinct Snapshots may legitimately share a digest.

diagnostic.remediation: Target Snapshots by Snapshot ID and use the manifest digest only to verify retained content integrity.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-28. Traversal: Snapshot-targeted live request traversal.

invariants.title: Deleted or stale Snapshot handle retargeted to equal content
invariants.statement: A Snapshot ID that no longer resolves returns a typed target-not-found result and is never resolved to a different Snapshot with equal manifest digest or equivalent content.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested Snapshot ID and the durable Snapshot record set including tombstones. Q2: the Snapshot record set including its tombstones is a Core durable record consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible live request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, because acceptance already binds the operation to a resource the caller never named. Q4: the retarget is committed by this request. It is expressible because content-addressed fallback is a plausible implementation choice, so it must be rejected rather than excluded by type.

diagnostic.remediation: Resolve Snapshot targets only by exact retained identity and return target-not-found for retired IDs.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-29. Traversal: Snapshot-targeted live request traversal.

invariants.title: Operation accepted without the exact target its kind seals
invariants.statement: Every accepted Operation records exactly the tagged target variant its operation kind requires, with every coordinate that variant seals present and resolved -- including the exact expected runtime epoch that every runtime-acting live mutation's target variant seals.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested method's declared target variant and the coordinates the submitted target carries, complete at live admission. Q2: the protected artefact is the accepted Operation record, a Core durable record, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L0 is the acceptance station and the last point at which an incomplete sealed target can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the request whose acceptance would commit the Operation. Merged from indices 5 and 16 (L1.D13, L2.D17) -- a general rule and its instance filed under different owners at one station.

diagnostic.remediation: Supply the tagged target variant declared for the requested method with all sealed coordinates populated, including the expected runtime epoch observed on the handle.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-05, IDENTITY-23, IDENTITY-25, LIFECYCLE-22. Traversal: live Sandbox, Process, Snapshot, and Fork mutation request traversal.

invariants.title: Process-targeted Operation retargeted during retry or reconciliation
invariants.statement: A Process-targeted Operation keeps the exact Process ID, Sandbox ID, and runtime epoch committed at its acceptance through every retry, adoption, and reconciliation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the committed Operation target record and the retarget the retry or reconciliation proposes; both are Core records at the live commit station. Q2: durable Operation records are Core. Q3: L1 is where the proposed rewrite would be committed and is therefore the last correct refusal point on this traversal. Q4: a system-originated reconciliation is filed at the same phase as its caller-originated twin, because origin is attribution and not an information set.

diagnostic.remediation: Reconcile only against the target committed at acceptance and create a linked successor Operation for any different target.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-26, LIFECYCLE-23. Traversal: Signal or Terminate live commit and reconciliation traversal.

invariants.title: Runtime-replacing result omits its previous or resulting epoch
invariants.statement: Every Operation result that replaces or creates a runtime records both the previous runtime epoch, or its explicit absence, and the resulting runtime epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the epoch held before this mutation and the epoch it committed, both present in Core records at the result-commit station; no post-launch observation is required, so this is not observed conformance. Q2: the Operation result record is Core. Q3: L1 is the commit that publishes the result; after it the caller can only infer continuity from mutable status. Q4: this result belongs to the live mutation whose traversal is described.

diagnostic.remediation: Record both the previous and resulting runtime epochs on every runtime-replacing or runtime-creating result.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-23, LIFECYCLE-46. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation result-commit traversal.

invariants.title: Attachment continuity conflated with runtime continuity
invariants.statement: Every lifecycle Operation able to change client attachment reports an explicit attachment outcome equivalent to preserved or reconnect-required, and that outcome never decides, substitutes for, or is decided by the runtime epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the attachment observation and the epoch decision recorded on the same result, both available at the result-commit station. Q2: the result record and epoch decision are Core. Q3: L1, because after the result is published a missing or conflated attachment outcome cannot be distinguished from preserved continuity. Q4: the conflation is committed by this Operation's own result.

diagnostic.remediation: Report attachment continuity as its own non-identity outcome and decide the epoch solely from proven runtime continuity.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-24. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation result-commit traversal.

invariants.title: Process record not permanently bound to one Sandbox runtime
invariants.statement: Every accepted Process receives a newly allocated Core Process ID permanently bound to exactly one Sandbox ID and runtime epoch, and that binding is never rewritten.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Exec request's runtime reference and the Process identity allocation record, both complete at the exec admission station. Q2: durable Process identity is Core. Q3: E0 is the last station where the binding can still be refused before the Process handle is published to the caller. Q4: a later rebinding attempt by reconciliation is a different act but consults this same committed binding, so it is defensively revalidated rather than separately filed here.

diagnostic.remediation: Allocate a fresh Core Process ID bound to the exact requested Sandbox ID and epoch, and never rebind it.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges LIFECYCLE-24, IDENTITY-01. Traversal: Exec acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Native execution identifier used as durable public identity
invariants.statement: Native PIDs, provider execution identifiers, provider resource identifiers, and VMM identities are recorded only as scoped decoded observations and never become or resolve durable public Sandbox, runtime, Process, Operation, or Snapshot identity.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the native identifiers the driver decodes and the public identity domains they are being written into; both are complete at the decoding boundary. Q2: decoding native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, which is runtime. Q3: D0 is the last station before decoded values reach authoritative Core records. Q4: the substitution is committed by the driver on this effect traversal, not by the caller's request.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep native identifiers in scoped protected evidence and resolve public resources only through Core-allocated identities.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-12. Traversal: driver decoding and effect-commit traversal.

invariants.title: Runtime epoch accepted as Create input
invariants.statement: The canonical Create request expresses no runtime epoch, leaving the first epoch server-allocated output-only state that no caller, native extension, or adapter can set, preserve, or reset.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the canonical Create request schema, complete at the create request surface. Q2: the creation request surface owns its input schema. Q3: C0 is the boundary that decodes the canonical request. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because the supported create surface, including its native-extension slots, offers no epoch-carrying field.

diagnostic.remediation: Read the allocated epoch from the Create result instead of attempting to supply one.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-01. Traversal: CreateSandbox request traversal.

invariants.title: Runtime epoch written by a live request
invariants.statement: A live request expresses the runtime epoch only as an expected-value precondition and never as an assignable field able to set, reset, preserve, or decrement it.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the live request schema and the read-only status of the epoch, complete at the live request surface. Q2: the live request surface owns its input schema. Q3: L0 is the decoding boundary for live requests. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because every live request type carries the epoch only in a precondition position.

diagnostic.remediation: Use the epoch as a precondition only and let the Core allocate every new runtime epoch.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-01, IDENTITY-05. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation request traversal.

invariants.title: Sandbox name mutated after Create
invariants.statement: The Sandbox name is fixed at Create, and no metadata, expiration, or other live update request can express a replacement name.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the update request schema for the two representation methods, complete at the live request surface. Q2: those request surfaces are live. Q3: L0 is where the update request is decoded. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because the metadata and expiration requests carry no name field at all, which is what prevents hidden release and rename races.

diagnostic.remediation: Create a new Sandbox with the desired alias rather than attempting to rename an existing one.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges TAXONOMY-17. Traversal: UpdateSandboxMetadata and SetSandboxExpiration request traversal.

invariants.title: Process identifier or output cursor used as an exec identity or authority coordinate
invariants.statement: Every output and event cursor on the exec branch is an observation position only, and the Core Process ID is the sole Process identity coordinate; neither is accepted in an identity, target, precondition, or authority position, and a native execution identifier is accepted in none of them.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the fact is the declared domain of each exec-branch coordinate at the boundary that decodes it, complete at the exec request surface. Q2: the invalid state is an expressible exec request, so the owner is `exec` under Criterion O. Q3: E0 is the decoding station and the last point at which a wrong-domain coordinate can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's exec or Process-control request. Split out of M8 because output cursors live at `process.status.output.cursor` on the exec branch and L0 and E1 are mutually unreachable (L0.D2).

diagnostic.remediation: Carry output and event cursors only in observation requests and use the Core Process ID as the sole Process identity coordinate.

invariants.notes: Packet E IDE family; discharges IDENTITY-07. Traversal: Exec and Process-control request traversal, at semantic decoding.

invariants.title: Create rejected after durable creation intent exists
invariants.statement: A CreateSandbox call returns a request rejection only while Core proves that no Operation, no dispatchable effect intent, no external invocation, and no recoverable accepted result exists; otherwise it is accepted and every later outcome is embedded in its Operation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the four acceptance-proof conditions over Core's own durable records, complete at the creation acceptance station without needing the resolved target runtime. Q2: durable acceptance records are Core. Q3: D0 is the last station on this traversal before an external effect exists, after which a rejection would deny a committed acceptance. Q4: the rejection would be returned by this same call.

diagnostic.remediation: Return a request rejection only before the acceptance commit and afterwards report every outcome inside the Operation.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-01. Traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Live request rejected after durable mutation intent exists
invariants.statement: A live Sandbox, Process-signal, Snapshot, or Fork mutation returns a request rejection only while Core proves that no Operation, no dispatchable effect intent, no external invocation, and no recoverable accepted result exists.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the same four acceptance-proof conditions read over this request's own durable records at the live admission station. Q2: durable acceptance is Core. Q3: L1 is the acceptance commit and the last station at which a rejection is still truthful. Q4: the create and exec surfaces never traverse L0, so filing one entry for all three would assert coverage on components that never see this pair.

diagnostic.remediation: Prove the four acceptance conditions before returning a request rejection and otherwise accept and report through the Operation.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-01. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Exec rejected after durable execution intent exists
invariants.statement: An Exec returns a request rejection only while Core proves that no Process, no dispatchable effect intent, no external invocation, and no recoverable accepted result exists.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the four acceptance-proof conditions read over the Process record and effect intent at the exec admission station. Q2: durable acceptance is Core. Q3: E1 is the Process acceptance commit and the last station at which a rejection is still truthful. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0 or L1, so this is a separate entry from the live-surface rule.

diagnostic.remediation: Prove the four acceptance conditions before returning a request rejection and otherwise accept and report through the Process.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-01. Traversal: Exec acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Launch dispatched before its acceptance commit
invariants.statement: No launch or other external creation effect is dispatched before Core atomically commits the Operation handle, canonical request and digest, preallocated Sandbox identity, idempotency binding, allocated runtime epoch, effect intent, and effect-authority epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the contents of the acceptance commit, all of which exist at the creation acceptance station; the resolved target runtime value is not needed to decide whether the commit happened first, so C0 is the earliest complete station rather than D0. Q2: the durable acceptance record is Core. Q3: D0 is the last station before the external effect is invoked. Q4: the dispatch belongs to this create traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Commit the full acceptance record, epoch allocation, and effect intent atomically before invoking any provider or driver effect.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-02, IDENTITY-02. Traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance and launch-dispatch traversal.

invariants.title: Live effect dispatched before its acceptance commit
invariants.statement: No live external effect is dispatched before Core atomically commits the Operation handle, canonical request and digest, sealed target with every applicable freshness precondition, idempotency binding, effect intent, and effect-authority epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the acceptance-commit contents for this live mutation, complete at the live admission station. Q2: the durable acceptance record is Core. Q3: L1 is the commit that must precede dispatch, so it is the last correct refusal point. Q4: the dispatch is performed for this same live request.

diagnostic.remediation: Commit the acceptance record and effect intent atomically before dispatching the live effect.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-02, IDENTITY-02. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation acceptance and dispatch traversal.

invariants.title: Exec dispatched before its acceptance commit
invariants.statement: No Exec is dispatched before Core atomically commits the Core Process ID, canonical request and digest, exact Sandbox runtime reference, idempotency binding, launch token, effect intent, and effect-authority epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the exec acceptance-commit contents, complete at the exec admission station. Q2: the durable Process record is Core. Q3: E1 is the commit that must precede dispatch; after dispatch an unrecorded execution cannot be reconciled by launch token. Q4: the dispatch belongs to this exec traversal, which never enters the live pair.

diagnostic.remediation: Durably allocate the Process ID and launch token and commit the acceptance record before dispatching the execution.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-02, TAXONOMY-10. Traversal: Exec acceptance and dispatch traversal.

invariants.title: Create replay rejected against current mutable state
invariants.statement: Idempotency lookup for a CreateSandbox request runs immediately after authorization and canonicalization and before target-state, capability, concurrency, capacity, and quota checks, so an equal replay recovers its original handle.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the idempotency coordinate, the stored binding, and the declared admission order, all complete at the create request surface. Q2: the idempotency binding and the declared ordered admission sequence are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: C0, because once a mutable-state error is returned the caller has lost the recovery path to its original handle. Q4: the misordering is committed by this request.

diagnostic.remediation: Resolve idempotency before evaluating mutable lifecycle, capacity, or quota preconditions.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-12, RESULT-15. Traversal: CreateSandbox admission traversal.

invariants.title: Live replay rejected against current mutable state
invariants.statement: Idempotency lookup for a live mutation runs immediately after authorization and canonicalization and before lifecycle-state, concurrency, capacity, and quota checks, so a retry of an accepted mutation recovers its original Operation instead of being rejected as invalid for the current state.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the idempotency coordinate, the stored binding, and the declared admission order at the live request surface. Q2: the stored binding is a Core durable record, which also makes this a boundary rejection rather than a dynamic preflight. Q3: L0, because a state-based rejection already destroys the recovery path. Q4: the misordering belongs to this request; the classic instance is a retried Start arriving after the Sandbox is already running.

diagnostic.remediation: Look up the idempotency coordinate before any mutable-state check and return the original Operation on equal replay.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-12, RESULT-15. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal.

invariants.title: Exec replay rejected against current mutable state
invariants.statement: Idempotency lookup for an Exec runs immediately after authorization and canonicalization and before execution-admission, concurrency, capacity, and quota checks, so an equal replay recovers its original Process.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the idempotency coordinate, the stored binding, and the declared admission order at the exec request surface. Q2: the stored binding is a Core durable record. Q3: E0, because an admission-based rejection loses the caller's route back to the accepted Process. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so it needs its own entry.

diagnostic.remediation: Resolve the Exec idempotency coordinate before evaluating execution admission or capacity.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-12, RESULT-15. Traversal: Exec admission traversal.

invariants.title: Live idempotency coordinate rebound to a different intent
invariants.statement: One authenticated scope, method, and idempotency key binds exactly one canonical request digest for its published recovery window, so an equal replay returns the original Operation and a conflicting replay is rejected without dispatching any effect.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored binding of coordinate to canonical digest to handle and the incoming digest; the consulted fact is a Core durable record, not request content, which fixes the owner as core rather than the request surface. Q2: the idempotency binding is a Core durable record. Q3: L0, because acceptance under a rebound key already produces a second effect. Q4: the create surface never traverses L0, so the creation-scope half of this rule cannot be asserted here and is filed as its own entry at `199`.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the conflicting replay with the typed idempotency conflict and dispatch nothing, or submit a new key.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges IDENTITY-08, RESULT-13, RESULT-14. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal.

invariants.title: Exec idempotency coordinate rebound to a different intent
invariants.statement: One authenticated scope, method, and idempotency key binds exactly one canonical Exec digest for its published recovery window, so an equal replay returns the original Process and a conflicting replay is rejected without dispatching any execution.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored Exec binding and the incoming canonical digest, both Core durable records. Q2: the binding is Core. Q3: E0, because acceptance under a rebound key already launches a second execution. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so the live entry cannot assert coverage here.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the conflicting Exec replay with the typed idempotency conflict and dispatch no execution.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges IDENTITY-08, RESULT-13, RESULT-14. Traversal: Exec admission traversal.

invariants.title: Canonical request identity includes transport or presentation fields
invariants.statement: The canonical request digest excludes transport-only fields, trace identifiers, and correlation metadata, and includes every field able to change target, authority, effect, policy, result, or postcondition.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the request encoding and the declared canonicalization domain, complete at the live request surface where the digest is computed. Q2: the canonical digest is a Core durable-record input. Q3: L0, because the digest is stored with the acceptance commit and a wrong domain makes both false conflicts and false replays permanent. Q4: the miscanonicalization is committed by the request being admitted; correlation metadata carries no deduplication or authorization meaning by construction.

diagnostic.remediation: Canonicalize over semantic fields only and keep trace and correlation metadata outside the digest.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges IDENTITY-07, IDENTITY-08, RESULT-13. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation canonicalization traversal.

invariants.title: Retired create idempotency record silently authorizes a new effect
invariants.statement: A CreateSandbox replay whose idempotency coordinate is retired or older than the published recovery window returns a recovery error carrying its tagged prior-acceptance evidence and never becomes a new accepted creation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the coordinate age, the published recovery window, the acceptance tombstone, and the retained result reference, all Core records available at the create request surface. Q2: the acceptance tombstone, the published recovery window, and the retained result reference are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: C0, because accepting it as new already authorizes a second creation. Q4: the conversion would be committed by this request.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the expired-record recovery error with its prior-acceptance evidence and require operator or observation recovery.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-15, RESULT-12. Traversal: CreateSandbox admission traversal.

invariants.title: Retired live idempotency record silently authorizes a new mutation
invariants.statement: A live mutation replay whose idempotency coordinate is retired or older than the published recovery window returns a recovery error carrying its tagged prior-acceptance evidence and never becomes a new accepted mutation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the coordinate age, the published window, tombstones, and any retained result reference, all Core durable records. Q2: retention and tombstones are Core. Q3: L0, because acceptance is itself the silent conversion. Q4: the create and exec surfaces never traverse this pair and therefore carry their own entries.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the expired-record recovery error and never treat an expired coordinate as proof that no effect occurred.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-15, RESULT-12. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal.

invariants.title: Retired exec idempotency record silently authorizes a new execution
invariants.statement: An Exec replay whose idempotency coordinate is retired or older than the published recovery window returns a recovery error carrying its tagged prior-acceptance evidence and never becomes a new accepted execution.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the coordinate age, the published window, tombstones, and any retained Process reference, all Core durable records. Q2: retention and tombstones are Core. Q3: E0, because acceptance already launches a second execution. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so this is filed separately.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the expired-record recovery error and require explicit observation before any new execution is formed.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-15, RESULT-12. Traversal: Exec admission traversal.

invariants.title: Terminal failed Operation automatically replayed as a new attempt
invariants.statement: An accepted terminal failure is recovered as the original Operation's outcome, and creating a genuinely new attempt requires a new idempotency key together with operation-specific authority to attempt it again.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored idempotency binding and the terminal outcome of the bound Operation, both Core durable records at the admission station. Q2: durable Operation records are Core. Q3: L0, because acceptance of the replay as a new attempt is itself the unauthorized second effect. Q4: a system-originated replay is filed at exactly the phase of its caller-originated twin, since origin is attribution and not an information set.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the original failed Operation on replay and require a new key plus explicit authority for a fresh attempt.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-16, RESULT-15. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal.

invariants.title: Cancellation request recorded as a cancellation fact
invariants.statement: An accepted cancellation request monotonically records cancel_requested on the existing Operation and allocates no new Operation, leaving that Operation the sole authority for its terminal outcome.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the existing Operation record and the cancellation intent commit, both Core records at the live acceptance station; proving exclusion of the effect is a different fact set carried by the outcome-legality entries. Q2: durable Operation records are Core. Q3: L1 is the intent commit, the last station at which an Operation-of-Operation or a premature cancelled outcome can still be refused. Q4: the terminal outcome is decided on the target Operation's own traversal, not here.

diagnostic.remediation: Record cancel_requested on the existing Operation and let that Operation publish the terminal outcome once exclusion is proven.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges IDENTITY-16, TAXONOMY-14, RESULT-22. Traversal: CancelOperation acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Representation and idempotency result committed separately
invariants.statement: An atomic Core-record update commits the new representation, its resulting revision, the idempotency binding, and the recoverable committed response in one commit, so an equal replay returns that response without applying the update again.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the prior revision, the requested representation, and the idempotency binding, all Core records complete at the live admission station. Q2: Core-owned representation records are Core. Q3: L1 is the single commit point; splitting it is only observable there. Q4: this update class has no dispatch or later traversal on which the split could be caught.

diagnostic.remediation: Commit representation, resulting revision, idempotency binding, and committed response in one atomic write.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-31. Traversal: UpdateSandboxMetadata and SetSandboxExpiration acceptance traversal.

invariants.title: Non-atomic record storage exposed for atomic update methods
invariants.statement: A Core deployment whose record storage cannot commit the representation and its idempotency result atomically fails admission for the atomic-update methods rather than advertising them or substituting a durable Operation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the configured storage's declared transactional capability and the method set being advertised, both complete at operator configuration. Q2: deployment storage selection and capability admission are operator-owned. Q3: O0 is the operator resolution boundary and the last station before the method is advertised. Q4: the caller's later request is a different traversal that would already be too late, so the refusal is filed here.

diagnostic.remediation: Fail build, startup, or capability admission closed instead of advertising the atomic-update methods on non-transactional storage.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges RESULT-31. Traversal: operator configuration and capability-admission traversal.

invariants.title: External effect attempted before its recovery classification is recorded
invariants.statement: Before each external effect attempt on the launch traversal Core durably records the attempt with its exact parameters together with one of the four locked recovery classes: no durable intent, provider idempotency token available, external identity discoverable for adoption, or none available.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the effect parameters plus the provider's currently available idempotency scope and identity discoverability, which are external provider state and must be determined before mutation rather than after. Q2: the durable effect-attempt record and its classification are Core. Q3: R0 is the last station before the launch result is interpreted, after which an unclassified attempt cannot be safely retried or adopted. Q4: the driver's obligation to prove native idempotency or exact adoption is the other half of a two-owner seam and is filed on the driver's own boundary.

diagnostic.remediation: Persist the effect-attempt record with its recovery class before dispatch, and report ambiguity with quarantine when no class applies.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges LIFECYCLE-43, RESULT-19, RESULT-20. Traversal: external effect-attempt traversal preceding launch dispatch.

invariants.title: Live external effect attempted before its recovery classification is recorded
invariants.statement: Before dispatching any external effect on the live-mutation traversal, Core durably records the attempt with its exact parameters together with one of the four locked recovery classes — no durable intent, provider idempotency token available, external identity discoverable for adoption, or none available — and reports ambiguity with quarantine when no class applies.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the effect parameters and the driver's declared effect class, together with the Core-held attempt record; all are available from live admission through the effect commit. Q2: the durable effect-attempt record and its classification are Core durable records. Q3: L1 is the last station at which refusing still prevents an unclassified live dispatch. Q4: the offending act is the live mutation's own dispatch. Added because `60` narrows to the launch branch, and D0→R0 reaches neither L1 nor E1 (L0.D8); this mirrors the three-way split already used for acceptance commits (`37` C0→D0, `38` L0→L1, `39` E0→E1).

diagnostic.remediation: Durably record the attempt and one of the four locked recovery classes before dispatching the live external effect, and quarantine the attempt as ambiguous when no class applies.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges LIFECYCLE-43, RESULT-19, RESULT-20. Traversal: live Sandbox mutation traversal, at external effect-attempt recording preceding dispatch.

invariants.title: Exec external effect attempted before its recovery classification is recorded
invariants.statement: Before dispatching any external effect on the Exec traversal, Core durably records the attempt with its exact parameters together with one of the four locked recovery classes — no durable intent, provider idempotency token available, external identity discoverable for adoption, or none available — and reports ambiguity with quarantine when no class applies.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the effect parameters and the driver's declared effect class, together with the Core-held attempt record; all are available from Exec admission through the dispatch commit. Q2: the durable effect-attempt record and its classification are Core durable records. Q3: E1 is the last station at which refusing still prevents an unclassified exec dispatch. Q4: the offending act is the Exec's own dispatch. Added because `60` narrows to the launch branch, and D0→R0 reaches neither L1 nor E1 (L0.D8); this mirrors the three-way split already used for acceptance commits (`37` C0→D0, `38` L0→L1, `39` E0→E1).

diagnostic.remediation: Durably record the attempt and one of the four locked recovery classes before dispatching the exec external effect, and quarantine the attempt as ambiguous when no class applies.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges LIFECYCLE-43, RESULT-19, RESULT-20. Traversal: Exec traversal, at external effect-attempt recording preceding dispatch.

invariants.title: Create idempotency coordinate rebound to a different intent
invariants.statement: One authenticated scope, method, and idempotency key binds exactly one canonical CreateSandbox request digest for its published recovery window; a replay under the same coordinate with a different canonical digest is refused as a conflict and dispatches no effect.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored idempotency binding and the canonical digest of the submitted request, both Core durable records at the creation acceptance station. Q2: idempotency binding and tombstone records are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so the owner is `core`. Q3: C0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a rebound coordinate from authorizing an effect. Q4: the offending act is the Create replay itself. Closes L3.D3: the create surface never traverses L0, so the live entry `46` could not cover it, and the cross-reference to a 'creation-scope entry' pointed at nothing in the 204.

diagnostic.remediation: Refuse a replay whose canonical digest differs from the one already bound to the coordinate, and use a fresh idempotency key for a different intent.

invariants.notes: Packet E OPA family; discharges IDENTITY-08, RESULT-13, RESULT-14. Traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal, at idempotency binding.

invariants.title: Launch Operation terminalized beyond its proven evidence
invariants.statement: A launch Operation commits `succeeded` only when every possibility remaining under Core's evidence satisfies its exact success postcondition with cancellation `notRequested` or proven `lost`, commits `failed` or `cancelled` only when no remaining possibility satisfies that postcondition, every possibility has `mutationAuthority = quiesced`, and residual effects are known, and otherwise commits `unknown` with its exact ambiguity variant.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the accumulated knowledge set for one accepted launch attempt, its cancellation causality, and the method-specific success predicate; that set is complete only at R1, where the launched runtime has been observed and probed. Q2: Core owns terminal Operation outcomes. Q3: R1 is the station that publishes the terminal outcome, so refusing an unproven arm there is still a correct product implementation. Q4: this is the launch traversal's own outcome, not a later operation's. `observed-conformance` because arm legality is provable only from post-launch evidence; the `mutationAuthority = quiesced` predicate and the cancellation causality lattice are required witnesses rather than separate entries. Filed as a self-pair on the launch traversal, never as C0->R1.

diagnostic.remediation: Commit `unknown` with its exact ambiguity variant unless the evidence proves the whole predicate of the chosen arm, including quiesced mutation authority and known residuals.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, RESULT-21, RESULT-22, RESULT-23, LIFECYCLE-47. Traversal: Create/Start/Restore launch traversal terminalizing at R1.

invariants.title: Live mutation Operation terminalized beyond its proven evidence
invariants.statement: A live Sandbox, Snapshot, or Process-targeted mutation Operation commits `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled` only when its exact evidence predicate for that arm holds over every remaining possibility, and otherwise commits `unknown`; a received cancellation request, an unresolved `cancellation = requested`, an internal timer expiry, or an RPC deadline never selects a definite arm.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the knowledge set, cancellation causality, and success predicate for one accepted live mutation; complete only at L1, where that mutation's effect evidence exists. Q2: Core owns terminal Operation outcomes. Q3: L1 publishes the outcome and is the last station on this traversal at which refusing an unproven arm is correct. Q4: the live mutation's own traversal. A single L1->T0 filing was rejected because it would bind the launch and exec branches to a pair they do not traverse in that direction; per-station filing keeps the coverage claim true. `observed-conformance` because the arm is provable only after the effect was attempted.

diagnostic.remediation: Leave the Operation `unknown` while cancellation is unresolved or mutation authority may still act; never promote a cancellation request or deadline into a terminal arm.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, IDENTITY-16, RESULT-21, RESULT-22, RESULT-23, LIFECYCLE-47. Traversal: One live mutation against an existing Sandbox, terminalizing at L1.

invariants.title: Exec dispatch outcome committed beyond its proven evidence
invariants.statement: An accepted Exec dispatch commits a terminal Process outcome only when every possibility remaining under Core's evidence satisfies that outcome's exact predicate with quiesced dispatch authority and known residuals; every other nonempty knowledge set leaves the Process in reconcilable `unknown`.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the evidence set for one accepted execution attempt against the Process success predicate; they first exist at E1, after dispatch. Q2: Core owns the durable Process record and which outcome it may commit; the driver's decoding of native termination evidence into a typed arm is a separate runtime-owned rule. Q3: E1 is where the Process record is terminalized, so refusal there is still correct. Q4: the Exec traversal's own outcome. `observed-conformance` because the knowledge set exists only after the launch effect was attempted.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep the Process `unknown` and reconcilable until exact evidence bound to the same launch token proves the committed outcome.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, RESULT-21, RESULT-22, LIFECYCLE-47. Traversal: One Exec request inside an existing Sandbox, terminalizing at E1.

invariants.title: Teardown Operation terminalized beyond its proven evidence
invariants.statement: A Stop, Delete, or other teardown Operation commits `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled` only when its exact evidence predicate holds over every remaining possibility, and otherwise commits `unknown`; a cleanup attempt, a missing observation, native resource absence, or a provider acknowledgement never substitutes for cleanup completion, target absence, descendant quiescence, or the required Core postcondition.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the teardown attempt's final evidence set, its residual obligations, and its cancellation causality; complete only at T0, the sink where teardown evidence is final. Q2: Core owns terminal Operation outcomes. Q3: T0 publishes the outcome and is the last station on this traversal. Q4: the teardown traversal's own outcome; cleanup carried out by a later linked Operation is filed on that Operation's traversal. `observed-conformance` because absence and quiescence are provable only from observed teardown evidence.

diagnostic.remediation: Report `unknown` while any descendant, orphan, or cleanup obligation may still act; never infer absence from a missing observation or an accepted cleanup call.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, TAXONOMY-14, LIFECYCLE-47. Traversal: Stop/Delete teardown traversal terminalizing at T0.

invariants.title: Terminal Operation result rewritten
invariants.statement: An Operation's committed terminal outcome and its payload are immutable, and later evidence, reconciliation, adoption, quarantine, or cleanup may only append a linked successor record that references the unchanged predecessor.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the existing terminal Operation record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records and no new observation is needed to refuse the rewrite. Q2: Core owns durable records and terminal outcomes. Q3: R1 is the launch-branch reconciliation/adoption traversal's own resolution station and the last point on that traversal at which the rewrite can be refused; `origin` is attribution, so a system-originated reconciliation is filed at the station its caller-originated twin traverses, and reconciliations that resolve at L1 or T0 are filed as their own per-station siblings rather than asserted here. Q4: the offending write belongs to the reconciling traversal, which is the traversal described here. `reject-at-boundary` rather than `observed-conformance`: immutability is decided from two stored records, not proved after launch; the reconciler's separate evidence-gathering discipline is a different obligation. The legal form -- appending a linked successor resolution record -- is this entry's required valid witness.

diagnostic.remediation: Append a linked successor resolution Operation instead of rewriting the predecessor's terminal outcome.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-18, LIFECYCLE-19, TAXONOMY-49, RESULT-24. Traversal: Launch-branch reconciliation/adoption traversal resolving against an existing terminal Operation, at R1.

invariants.title: Compensation represented as rollback
