invariants.statement: A compensating effect recorded on the teardown or cleanup traversal is recorded as a new forward effect with its own durable record, evidence, and outcome, and never as erasure, reversal, or negation of the compensated Operation's external history -- including when in-sandbox state was restored from a Snapshot or filesystem capture.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the compensated Operation's terminal record and the compensating effect's own record; the representation rule reads those two records at final evidence, so T0 is the earliest station where both exist. Q2: Core owns durable records and terminal outcomes; the D0-time declaration of a compensable effect class is a different fact set and is absorbed by the recovery-classification entry. Q3: T0 is the sink where the compensation record is published, and refusing a rollback representation there is still correct. Q4: the compensating traversal's own record. `reject-at-boundary` because the over-claim is visible in the two records without any further probe. The forbidden inference `filesystem restoration as external-effect rollback` is carried here as a required invalid witness: restoring in-sandbox state never claims that an email, network call, or payment was undone.

diagnostic.remediation: Record compensation as a new linked forward effect with its own outcome; never mark the compensated Operation or its external effects as reversed.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges LIFECYCLE-44, RESULT-20. Traversal: Compensating-effect traversal recording against a prior Operation on the teardown or cleanup traversal, at T0.

invariants.title: Observation deadline mutating or terminalizing its target
invariants.statement: An observation, wait, or watch deadline ends only that observation and never cancels, mutates, terminalizes, requests cancellation of, or advances the durable state of the observed Sandbox, Operation, or Snapshot.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the observation's own deadline and the identity of the observed durable record; both are complete at the observation request surface, and no effect evidence is required. Q2: Core owns the durable records whose state the deadline must not touch. Q3: L0 is where the observation is served and returned; an observation has no acceptance commit, so refusing the mutation there is the only correct implementation. Q4: an expiry-driven state change caused by a different operation is filed on that operation's traversal. `reject-at-boundary` because the deadline and the record are both known locally.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the observation result with the latest resource and an explicit condition-met flag; leave the observed record unchanged.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-17, RESULT-30. Traversal: One observation (Get/List/Wait) against an existing Sandbox, Operation, or Snapshot, at L0.

invariants.title: Interrupted effect attempt resolved without its committed intent
invariants.statement: An effect attempt interrupted after dispatch is resolved only by evidence bound to its own committed effect intent, launch token, exact external identity, and authority epoch, and is otherwise terminalized `unknown`; it is never resolved by a fresh attempt, by a differently identified native execution, or by assuming the attempt's outcome.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the durably committed effect intent, the dispatch record, and whatever evidence can be bound to them; they first exist together at R0, immediately after dispatch. Q2: Core owns the durable effect-attempt record and the terminal outcome; the driver's declaration and proof of native idempotency or exact adoption is a separate runtime-owned rule at D0. Q3: R1 is the last station on this traversal at which refusing an unbound resolution is still correct, because the outcome is published there. Q4: the interrupted attempt's own traversal. `reject-at-boundary`: the binding check compares recorded identities and needs no external-state preflight.

diagnostic.remediation: Reconcile using the same committed intent and launch token, or terminalize the Operation `unknown`; never dispatch a second attempt to resolve the first.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, LIFECYCLE-43, RESULT-19. Traversal: Launch traversal resuming an interrupted effect attempt between dispatch (R0) and terminalization (R1).

invariants.title: Ambiguous launch outcome used as successor-effect permission
invariants.statement: A launch Operation that terminalized `unknown` authorizes no relaunch, replacement, or adoption effect against the same intent, and any successor launch requires an independently proven fencing boundary, an exact adoption identity, or a newly authorized caller request with its own accepted intent.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the published terminal `unknown` outcome and the proposed successor effect's authorization basis; both exist at R1 once the outcome is committed. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes and effect authority. Q3: R1 is the station that would grant the successor, so refusing there is correct. Q4: where the successor is itself a fully separate accepted operation, its admission is filed on that operation's traversal; this entry constrains only the inference drawn at the ambiguous launch's own resolution station. `reject-at-boundary` because the terminal record and the successor's proof set are both Core-held.

diagnostic.remediation: Gather fencing or exact adoption proof, or require a new caller request with a new idempotency key; never treat `unknown` as permission to launch again.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, RESULT-19. Traversal: Launch traversal at its terminalization station, R1.

invariants.title: Ambiguous live outcome used as successor-effect permission
invariants.statement: A live mutation Operation that terminalized `unknown` authorizes no repeated, replacement, or compensating external effect against the same target and epoch until fenced evidence, exact adoption identity, or a newly authorized request establishes the successor's authority.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the live mutation's terminal `unknown` record and the proposed successor's authority basis; complete at L1. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes and effect authority. Q3: L1 is the resolution station for this traversal. Q4: a genuinely new caller-authored mutation is a different traversal and is admitted on its own facts; this entry forbids only Core-initiated replacement from the ambiguity itself. Filed separately from the launch station because a single filing would claim that the launch and exec components revalidate a pair they do not traverse. `reject-at-boundary`.

diagnostic.remediation: Quarantine or reconcile the target under a linked Operation; do not re-dispatch the same external effect on the strength of the ambiguity.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, RESULT-19. Traversal: One live mutation against an existing Sandbox, at its terminalization station L1.

invariants.title: Ambiguous teardown outcome used as cleanup or destruction permission
invariants.statement: A Stop or Delete Operation that terminalized `unknown`, or `failed` with residual obligations, authorizes no assumed-complete cleanup, no identity release, and no successor destructive effect until an actor holding current authority durably discharges each exact residual obligation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the teardown Operation's terminal record, its enumerated residual obligations, and the proposed successor's authority; complete at T0. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes, retention, and the release of identities. Q3: T0 is the sink where the successor would be authorized. Q4: a later cleanup Operation is a different traversal and carries its own admission facts; this entry constrains only the inference made at the ambiguous teardown's own station. `reject-at-boundary` because both the residual record and the successor's authority are Core-held.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep the residual obligations open and observable, and discharge them under a linked cleanup Operation with current authority before any further destructive effect.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-09, RESULT-19. Traversal: Stop/Delete teardown traversal at T0.

invariants.title: Launch-branch compensating effect represented as rollback
invariants.statement: A compensating effect on the launch traversal is recorded as a new forward effect with its own durable record, evidence, and outcome, never as erasure, reversal, or negation of the compensated Operation's external history.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the compensated Operation's external effect ledger and the compensating effect's own Operation record, both Core durable records at the launch-result station. Q2: the Operation record and its external effect ledger are Core-owned. Q3: R1 is the last station on the launch traversal at which a rollback representation can be refused. Q4: the offending act belongs to the launch traversal, not the teardown traversal that `66` now covers. Added under L0.D12 as the launch-branch sibling; the live and exec compensation strategies are carried by A9/A10's four locked recovery classes.

diagnostic.remediation: Record launch-branch compensation as a new linked forward effect with its own durable record, evidence, and outcome; never mark the compensated Operation or its external effects as reversed.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges LIFECYCLE-44, RESULT-20. Traversal: launch-traversal compensating-effect recording against a prior Operation, at R1.

invariants.title: Terminal Operation result rewritten on a live reconciliation traversal
invariants.statement: An Operation's committed terminal outcome and its payload are immutable on the live mutation traversal, and later evidence, reconciliation, adoption, quarantine, or cleanup resolving at the live outcome station may only append a linked successor record that references the unchanged predecessor.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the existing terminal Operation record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records available at the live outcome station and no new observation is needed to refuse the rewrite. Q2: durable Operation records and terminal outcomes are the control plane's own artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: L1 is the live traversal's own resolution station and the last point on that traversal at which the rewrite can be refused. Q4: the offending write belongs to the live reconciliation traversal described here; the launch-branch station is `51` and the teardown station is the T0 sibling. `reject-at-boundary`: immutability is decided from two stored records, not proved after an effect. Added because `51`'s traversal was narrowed to the launch branch and a reconciliation entering at L0 never reaches R1.

diagnostic.remediation: Append a linked successor resolution Operation instead of rewriting the predecessor's terminal outcome.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-18, LIFECYCLE-19, TAXONOMY-49, RESULT-24. Traversal: Live reconciliation/adoption traversal resolving against an existing terminal Operation, at L1.

invariants.title: Terminal Operation result rewritten on a teardown or cleanup reconciliation traversal
invariants.statement: An Operation's committed terminal outcome and its payload are immutable on the teardown and cleanup traversal, and later evidence, reconciliation, adoption, quarantine, or cleanup resolving at teardown may only append a linked successor record that references the unchanged predecessor.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the existing terminal Operation record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records available at the teardown sink and no new observation is needed to refuse the rewrite. Q2: durable Operation records and terminal outcomes are the control plane's own artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: T0 is the teardown traversal's sink and the last point at which the rewrite can be refused. Q4: the offending write belongs to the teardown or cleanup traversal described here; the launch-branch station is `51` and the live station is the L1 sibling. `reject-at-boundary`: immutability is decided from two stored records. Added because `51`'s traversal was narrowed to the launch branch and a teardown or cleanup reconciliation never reaches R1.

diagnostic.remediation: Append a linked successor resolution Operation instead of rewriting the predecessor's terminal outcome.

invariants.notes: Packet E PRF family; discharges IDENTITY-18, LIFECYCLE-19, TAXONOMY-49, RESULT-24. Traversal: Teardown/cleanup reconciliation traversal resolving against an existing terminal Operation, at T0.
